title: Cross-cycle allocation and canary cadence for Hosted API + Model Lineup
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Objective: Create a cross-quarter roadmap play that codifies how we allocate capacity and stage canary rollouts for hosted API model rotations. The goal is to reduce customer-visible regressions during model swaps, make capacity hedging explicit, and provide a prescriptive cadence teams can follow for Q2/Q3 releases.

Scope: Hosted API endpoints (public tiers + enterprise), model catalog rotations (major-version swaps and quantized variants), rollout tooling (console + API flags), and operational runbooks for rollback and mitigation. Excludes private/VPC on-prem upgrades and Dedicated capacity billing changes.

Success metrics (trade-offs):
- Regression rate (quality alerts per 10k requests) <= 0.5x baseline during canary windows.
- Time-to-failover for degraded models < 3 minutes for automatic fallbacks.
- Reserved capacity buffer configured per tranche reduces dropped requests during surge by >= 60%.
- Release velocity: reduce ad-hoc hotfix rollbacks by 30% vs prior quarter.

Proposed cadence and allocations:
- Phase 0 (Alignment, 2 weeks): finalize model swap roster and assign capacity hedges per endpoint (gold/silver/bronze).
- Phase 1 (Canary warm-start, 1 week): route 0.5-1% of traffic tied to synthetic prompt-sets and staging key customers.
- Phase 2 (Incremental ramp, 3-7 days): automated ramp to 5%, 20%, 50% with metric gates at each step.
- Phase 3 (Full swap + stabilization, 48-72h): open rollout to 100% with KV cache priming and adaptive batching adjustments.

Metric gates and triggers:
- Latency P95 increase > 20% → pause ramp and auto-scale dedicated pool (if available).
- Eval prompt-set quality drop (BLEU/ROUGE-style surrogate) > configured threshold → rollback to previous variant.
- Error rate delta > 2x baseline → immediate rollback and incident bridge.

Operational tools and data needs:
- Route key-level traffic slices in Console with linked dashboards (token-level cost + latency).
- Canary prompt-sets and golden traces stored in the eval repo (linked).
- Autoscale policies per tranche and pre-warmed p99 tail pools.

Stakeholders: PM (Ava Patel), Runtime Eng (Marcus Chen), Observability (Leah Murphy), Solutions Eng (Ravi Singh), Design (Nora Kim), Legal & Security (Compliant review required).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-conservative hedges cause wasted reserved capacity. Mitigation: Model-specific historical load analysis and weekly hedge tuning.
- Risk: Canary prompt-sets not representative. Mitigation: Customer-sourced test keys and higher-weighted enterprise traffic sampling.
- Risk: KV cache priming latency spike. Mitigation: staggered priming with synthetic priming traffic and cache warmup windows.

Deliverables:
- Roadmap doc + decision ledger (Confluence link).
- Canary runbook + rollback checklist.
- Console UI changes for tranche allocations (design spec).
- One pilot rotation for a low-risk endpoint (metrics dashboard).

Links to artifacts:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/pages/PM-24689-roadmap-canary-cadence
- Design spec: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/designs/PM-24689-canary-ux-v1
- Eval repo prompt-sets: https://git.internal.redwood/evals/canary-prompt-sets
- Pilot dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/hosted-api/pilot-PM-24689

Notes: This approach intentionally balances engineering work and product guardrails so we can scale model rotations across endpoints without manual triage on each swap.
